correctness.rationale: For all finite n>=2 under positive known immigration/recovery, calibrated global contact scaling and strictly bidirectional support, the derivative of the stationary law is derived uniquely from the centered Bernoulli eigenbasis and differentiated stationarity equation. Exact formulas for M_i and C_ij then give undirected support. Writing a_{j->i}=p_j beta_{ji}, pair observations fix each edge sum and node observations fix each incoming sum; the remaining signed-incidence system has nullity m-n+c. Strict positivity supports local ambiguities on each cycle and leaf peeling reconstructs rates exactly on forests. The attached standard-library exact-rational checker independently corroborates the equations on sampled finite chains, without using finite checks to prove the general theorem.

value.rationale: For a well-defined epidemiological inverse experiment with known baseline rates, the theorem separates undirected contact-structure identification from directed-transmission identifiability. It identifies a sharp and topologically interpretable loss of information equal to cycle rank, supplies constructive complete recovery on trees/forests and shows that even complete first-order joint observations cannot overcome the circulation obstruction. This is a motivated structural boundary with a concrete inverse-problem application, not a mere textbook sign calculation or arbitrary finite instance.
